answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The nadir multiplier is published, charged in umber, and dawn lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3013 identities would post 1307 proofs and burn roughly 7 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
